title: Complete endgame mastery: a DEM-level exam
summary: Mixed tablebase-verified test positions across all chapters of Dvoretsky's Endgame Manual, plus play-outs against full-strength defence.

steps.md:
## The exam

DEM-level knowledge means you know the result **and** the method of the key positions in every chapter: pawn endings, knight and bishop endings, opposite and same-coloured bishops, rook endings, rook v minor pieces, queen endings and other material relationships. Answer each question below without moving pieces; all answers are tablebase-verified.

steps.question: Chapter 1 (pawn endings). White to move: trebuchet on d5/d6. Result?
steps.explain: Mutual zugzwang: the side to move loses (tablebase).

steps.question: Chapter 5 (opposite-coloured bishops). White to move: pawns on b5 and h5. Result?
steps.explain: Tablebase: White wins, but only with 1.h6!; other moves allow ...Be3 blockading both pawns.

steps.question: Chapter 9 (rook endings). Black to move: Vancura position. Result?
steps.explain: Tablebase: draw; the rook attacks a6 from the side.

steps.question: Chapter 11 (rook v bishop). White to move: black king on a8 with a light-squared bishop. Result?
steps.explain: Tablebase: White mates in 2 — the wrong corner.

steps.question: Chapter 12 (queen endings). White to move: queen against c-pawn on the 7th, white king far away. Result?
Chapter 13 (other material). White to move: queen against rook and pawn in the f7/e6 fortress. Result?

steps.prompt: Play-out 1: Saavedra against full-strength defence. Win (tablebase: mate in 26).
Play-out 2: R+B v R, second-rank defence. Hold for 40 moves against full-strength attack.
Play-out 3: K+B+N v K. Mate within 40 moves (tablebase: mate in 30).

steps.md:
## Assignment

- Work through DEM chapter by chapter: 2 chapters per month, all positions solved before reading the solution, then checked with the tablebase in the **Analysis** board.
- Every month, repeat this exam until you score 100% and win/hold all play-outs.
